2027-02-26.title: Third Friday of the Great Fast
2027-02-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The mind set on the Spirit is life
2027-02-26.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). A Friday of abstinence from meat; the Way of the Cross is prayed in parishes and homes.
2027-02-26.verse: There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
theo: After the flood God speaks to Noah and binds himself by a promise, not only to Noah's family but “with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the domestic animals, and every animal of the earth with you.” He gives a sign: “I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.” The Hebrew word for the rainbow is the same as for a warrior's bow; God hangs up his weapon in the sky. And the sign is for God himself: “When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.” God binds himself to remember. The second reading tells how the walls of Jericho fell, not by siege engines but by obedience. Seven priests with seven trumpets walk before the ark, around the city, once a day for six days, and the people are told: “You shall not shout or let your voice be heard, nor shall you utter a word, until the day I tell you to shout.” On the seventh day they go round seven times; the trumpets sound, the people shout, “and the wall fell down flat.” Rahab and her family are spared “because she hid the messengers”. These pages of conquest are hard to read, and the Church reads them in the light of Christ, not as a pattern for treating people but as a picture of the walls of sin that fall before patient, silent obedience. During these weeks pilgrims climb Malayattoor hill, where tradition says St Thomas prayed, many carrying wooden crosses, step after step, calling on the golden cross. Like the circling of Jericho, Lenten prayer is often slow and repeated, and its fruit comes on a day we do not choose.

Paul opens the eighth chapter of Romans with the most freeing sentence a sinner can hear: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.” What the law could not do, God did, “by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh.” The choice before us is a matter of where we set our minds: “To set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.” In the Gospel the Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, bring Jesus a riddle about a woman married in turn to seven brothers: whose wife will she be? Jesus answers: “Is not this the reason you are wrong, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?” The risen life is not this life repeated; it is new. And he goes back to the burning bush, where God called himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, long after they had died: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.” On this Friday we walk the Way of the Cross to the tomb, but the tomb is not the end of the road. Those we have lost are alive to God, and we pray for them in that hope.
outline: Ask: what wall in my life has not yet fallen?
Point 1 · The bow in the clouds
The mind set on the Spirit is life and peace.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
live: Pray the Way of the Cross today with as little talk as possible before and after.
Name the departed of your family at the end of today's prayer, and visit their graves if you can.
2027-02-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, in you there is no condemnation. Remember your everlasting covenant with us, as you remembered Noah; bring down the walls of our sin through patient obedience; set our minds on the Spirit, who gives life and peace. You are God of the living: give eternal rest to our departed and bring us all to the resurrection. Amen.
altar: The rainbow was the sign of the covenant with Noah; at the Holy Qurbana Christ gives us the cup of the new covenant in his blood, and God remembers us for ever.

quick: God hangs his bow in the clouds and promises to remember his covenant.
Jericho falls through patient obedience; Lenten prayer is often slow and repeated.
No condemnation in Christ; God is the God of the living.
2027-02-26.action: Pray the Way of the Cross today in silence, and name your departed at the end.
2027-02-26.question: Do I still live under condemnation, when Christ has set me free?

family.explain: After the great flood God made a promise to Noah and to every animal: never again will a flood destroy the earth. God put a rainbow in the sky as a sign. When we see a rainbow, we can remember that God always keeps his promises.
family.intention: We pray for our family members who have died, that they may live with God.
family.ask: Ask: “What promise of God shall we thank him for tonight?”

illus: After the Way of the Cross on a Lenten Friday, a grandmother in Kuravilangad took her small grandson to the cemetery to light a candle at her husband's grave. The boy asked: is Appachan dead? She thought for a while and said: his body is sleeping here, but Jesus says God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. That is why we bring a light and not only flowers. The boy carefully shielded the flame from the wind all the way to the grave.

pm.open: Lord God, you remember your covenant for ever. Remember us now as we pray. Amen.
share: I will remember my covenant (Genesis 9:15). When has God been faithful to me though I was not faithful to him?
You shall not shout until the day I tell you (Joshua 6:10). Can I keep praying even when nothing seems to change?
He is God not of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). How does this change the way I remember my departed?
pm.resp: Lord, remember us in your kingdom.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim that in Christ there is no condemnation.
For those who carry the burden of guilt and cannot believe they are forgiven.
For pilgrims climbing Malayattoor and all who keep the Way of the Cross.
For our departed relatives and friends.
For our group, that we may set our minds on the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to your covenant and the God of the living. Free us from condemnation, keep us patient in prayer, and raise us up with all our dead. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, after the flood God set his bow in the clouds as a sign of the covenant (Genesis 9:13). God hung up his weapon in the sky and promised: I will remember. Our God is a God who remembers his promises.

The walls of Jericho fell not by force but by obedience: seven days of walking in silence around the city, and then a shout. Lenten prayer is like that. We walk the Way of the Cross, Friday after Friday, and the walls of sin fall on a day we do not choose.

Paul gives us the most freeing word a sinner can hear: there is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:1). Set your mind on the Spirit, and you will find life and peace.

Jesus tells the Sadducees that God is not God of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). Our Way of the Cross ends at a tomb, but the tomb is not the end. Let us pray today for our departed, who are alive to God. Amen.
kids: Children, after the flood God put a rainbow in the sky as a promise. God always keeps his promises! And Jesus tells us that people who die in God's love are alive with him.

intro: Theme: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
The rainbow covenant, the patient obedience that brought down Jericho, freedom from condemnation, and the God of the living.

sub: A weapon hung in the sky.
q: I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
And he did the same with the cup after supper, saying, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for three promises he has kept in your life.

sub: The law of the Spirit of life.
The mind set on the Spirit.
q: Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: If an old sin still weighs on you after confession, hand it to Christ today and believe his pardon.

sub: Our dead are alive to him.
q: He said further, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
He is God not of the dead, but of the living; you are quite wrong.”
points.apply: Pray for your departed by name today, and visit a grave if you can.

concl: God remembers his covenant, and in Christ there is no condemnation.
Walk patiently like Israel around Jericho, and remember that the road of the Cross leads to the God of the living.
2027-02-26.resolve: Pray the Way of the Cross today, and end it with a prayer for your departed.
